sitemapEmpiricalAudit.thesisVerification: Confirmed: raw competitor sitemap URL counts heavily overstate unique English calendar articles due to multi-locale translations, tag/pagination archives, release notes, and multi-product blogs.

domainsInspected.notes: 1,276 of 1,546 URLs are /de/, /es/, /fr/, /it/, /pt/ translations (~70 blog posts and ~61 guides per locale). Of the 270 English URLs, ~145 are blog posts/guides, including general task-app comparisons (ClickUp, Linear, Todoist, Asana).

1,081 of 1,305 URLs are /de/, /es/, /fr/, /it/, /ja/ translations. Of the 224 English URLs, ~30 are monthly product update announcements, ~14 are /compare/ pages, ~9 are /use-cases/, and ~135 are English how-to/blog articles.

Includes 73 /blog/tag/ archives and 52 /blog/page/ pagination URLs. Of 783 actual blog posts, only ~87 are calendar/scheduling-related, and several cannibalize each other (e.g., daily-planner, best-daily-planner-app, best-daily-planner-apps, daily-schedule, daily-schedule-template).

Excludes 35 BusyContacts docs. Includes 191 specific troubleshooting FAQs (/docs/faqs/), 71 BusyCal Mac docs, 36 BusyCal iOS docs, 11 comparisons, and 9 Bookings docs. Strongest model for granular, non-overlapping technical troubleshooting FAQs.
96 English blog posts in post-sitemap.xml + 32 product pages + 123 help articles in help.calendarbridge.com.
Most of the 513 English blog posts cover PDF Expert, Spark, Scanner Pro, and Documents. Only 68 mention Calendars, and >40 of those are legacy release notes or promo-code giveaways.
412 posts in post-sitemap.xml (mostly recipes and family lifestyle tips) + 287 pages in page-sitemap.xml (including /support/ articles).

scaleFeasibilityAndTaxonomy.honestAssessment: A narrow 'how to sync iPhone calendar' scope only supports ~180–250 distinct articles before synonym/device cannibalization occurs. To reach 1,100 genuinely unique English articles where every page answers a distinct user question with verifiable mechanics, we must structure the 1,027 new articles across 10 orthogonal, rule-driven clusters.
antiCannibalizationRules: Never create separate pages for iPhone vs iPad vs Apple Watch unless the operating system settings path, UI constraint, or sync architecture genuinely differs (e.g., watchOS 11 7-day window vs iPadOS split-screen month grid).
Never create separate pages for synonyms ('merge calendars', 'combine calendars', 'unify calendars') or modifier stuffing ('free', 'best', '2026', 'no ads').

Every page must pass the 'Distinct Rule / Artifact Gate': it must contain a unique protocol/permission matrix, a mathematical schedule cycle table, a deterministic troubleshooting isolation test, or an interactive calculator/validator not duplicated on any other route.
Every topic must declare its closest existing or planned neighbor (existingOverlapSlug) and an explicit boundary statement.
